info.title: Model Bank API
info.summary: The Model Bank's HTTP surface: the customer BFF, the console routes an operator drives, and the health check.
info.description:
Two servers share one process and one host. The customer BFF under `/v1/` serves the banking app: every response is a **screen tree** (`Screen`), rendered by the Flutter shell or as HTML for a browser, so a client interprets screens, not endpoints. Everything outside `/v1/` is the staff web; its HTML pages are not in this document, only the console routes another program drives (gobank-deploy's upgrade drill and performance runs) and `/about.json`, which it reads.

**Content negotiation.** A `/v1/` screen is JSON unless the request's `Accept` lists `text/html` and not `application/json`, when it is the same screen rendered as an HTML document. Errors follow the same rule: a browser gets the accompanying screen rendered, a JSON client gets `Error` with the screen under `screen`.

**Sessions.** `POST /v1/login` answers a JSON client with a bearer token and a browser with the `mb_session` cookie. The customer's identity always comes from the session, never from the request. A console route is reached with the operator token (`GOBANK_API_TOKEN`) as a bearer, or by a signed-in admin's `staff_session` cookie.

tags.name: customer
tags.description: The customer app's screens and session, under /v1/.

tags.name: console
tags.description: The simulation console as another program drives it; HTML pages of the staff web are not documented.

get.description: Answers as soon as the process serves HTTP. No session.
The OpenAPI document the running process was built with. No session.
The front door: a form whose `submit` is `POST /v1/login`. No session. The deployment's login note is the screen's text.

post.description: Checks the customer ID and password and opens a session. A JSON client gets the token and the home screen; a form post or a browser gets the `mb_session` cookie and is sent to the home screen. Five failures for one customer ID or from one address in fifteen minutes lock that key for the rest of the window.

303.description: Logged in (form or browser): the `mb_session` cookie is set and the browser is sent to `/v1/screen/accounts`.

401.description: Unknown customer ID or wrong password (`bad_credentials`), with the login screen carrying the notice.

429.description: Too many attempts for this customer ID or from this address (`rate_limited`); `Retry-After` says how long.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next attempt is accepted.

post.description: Ends the session. A browser's cookie is cleared and it is sent to the login screen; a JSON client gets the login screen.

get.description: The screen the app lands on: a hero with the net position and a row per account, each opening its product screen.
The customer's transactions, newest first, one page at a time.
The account's details (sort code, number, rate, balance) and its own transactions, one page at a time. `index` is the account's position in the customer's list on the home screen.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The account's index in the customer's accounts.

get.description: The version and schema this process runs, the console settings, the run's position and the restart record. gobank-deploy's upgrade drill reads it before and after each redeploy to compare the position and read the downtime off the newest restart row; a performance run reads the two rates under `sim`. No session.

post.description: The simulation runs day after day at the settings' day length until stopped.
The run stops after the day in progress.
Runs one business day while the run is stopped.
Empties the bank and starts again on its opening day. Settings are kept.

Opens `n` customers with the product mix the simulation uses, in the background; `sim.adding_customers` and `sim.customers_per_sec` on `/about.json` follow the batch. `n` is read from the form or the query.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: How many customers to add; zero or absent adds none.

post.description: The customer ceiling, the payments the generator sends a day, and the day length. Each is read from the form or the query; a day length that does not parse leaves the current one. The day length set here is the run's and outlives the process.

parameters.name: max_customers
parameters.description: The customer count the run stops adding at.

parameters.name: payments_per_day
parameters.description: Payments the generator sends each simulated day.

parameters.name: day_length
parameters.description: Wall-clock length of a simulated day; `0s` runs flat out.

303.description: Applied; the browser is sent to the settings page.

customerBearer.description: The token `POST /v1/login` returned to a JSON client. Sessions last eight hours and expire after fifteen idle minutes.

customerCookie.name: mb_session
customerCookie.description: The session cookie `POST /v1/login` set for a browser, scoped to `/v1`.

operatorToken.description: The deployment's operator token (`GOBANK_API_TOKEN`): another program driving the console. A wrong token is refused outright (401), never sent to the login page.

staffSession.name: staff_session
staffSession.description: A signed-in staff user's session, from the staff web's login page. The console routes need the admin or operator role.

page.name: page
page.description: The page of transactions, from 1; anything else is page 1.

Screen.description: The screen, as JSON or, for a browser, as an HTML document.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be read, or the login fields were empty or too long (`bad_request`).

Unauthenticated.description: No session, or one that has expired (`unauthenticated`): the login screen comes with the error. A browser is sent to `/v1/screen/login` instead (303).

Internal.description: The bank could not answer (`internal`); the cause is in the server log, never in the response.

BackToDashboard.description: Done; the browser is sent to the dashboard.

InvalidToken.description: The bearer token is not the operator token. Without any credential a browser is sent to the staff login page (303) instead.

Forbidden.description: The signed-in user's role may not do this.

error.description: A stable code a client can switch on.

screen.description: The screen to show with the error, when there is one: the login screen with its notice.

token.description: The session token, sent back as a bearer.

expires_at.description: When the session ends whatever happens; it also ends after fifteen idle minutes.

screen.description: The home screen, so the client has nothing more to fetch.

Screen.description: One screen of the app as a tree the client renders: a title, a body of components top to bottom, and the tab bar when the screen has one. `schema` is the tree's version; a client refuses a version it does not know.

path.description: The GET path that returns this screen.

back.description: Where the back control goes, when the screen has one.

Component.description: One element of a screen's body. `type` says which fields carry meaning: hero (title as label, value, pairs, tone); row (icon, title, subtitle, value, note, tone, action); tx (as row, no action); heading (text); text (text, tone); details (title, pairs); form (fields, title as the submit label, action.submit); button (title, tone, action).

value.description: Money already formatted for display, e.g. `£1,234.56`; the client never does arithmetic on it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the money a row or tx shows; the renderer picks the glyph by it.

Action.description: What a tap does: exactly one of the three.

screen.description: GET this path and show the screen it returns.

submit.description: POST the form's values to this path.

active.description: The key of the tab this screen belongs to.

screen.description: The GET path the tab opens.

name.description: The form value's name when submitted.

Tone.description: How the client colours the component; empty is neutral.

Icon.description: The glyph the client draws; empty is none.

schema.description: Each component's schema version in the database this process opened.

restarts.description: The restart record, newest first, ten rows at most.

AboutSim.description: The run as it is now, with the two rates a performance run reads.

clock.description: The bank's clock now (simulated time), UTC.

warp.description: Simulated seconds per wall second; 0 when flat out.

customers_per_sec.description: The live rate while a batch add runs, else the last batch's.

account_days_per_12h.description: Account days per 12h at the pass's measured whole-day rate.

last_day_duration.description: A Go duration; empty before the first day.

last_day_accounts.description: The accounts the last whole day ran over.

day_refused.description: Why the bank would not follow the clock when last asked; absent when it did.

next_event.description: The event the run loop waits for, e.g. `payment at 2020-03-04T10:32:00Z`; absent when stopped.

AboutOwed.description: What the bank owed when last asked; a drill waits for `at_rest`.

days.description: Business days the clock has passed that the bank has not run.

unprojected.description: Accounts whose position is behind the ledger.

events.description: Root events due and not done: cascades in progress.

AboutPosition.description: The bank's position: what the dashboard leads with.

day_count.description: Business days run since the bank opened.

savings.description: Formatted as the dashboard shows it.

lending.description: Formatted as the dashboard shows it.

AboutRestart.description: One row of the restart record, read with the row before it.

downtime.description: A Go duration; empty when unknown.

intact.description: Day and customers equal across the stop; null when the previous row cannot say.
